o: Complete a timed assessment independently and show all working.
Use OCR command words and mark allocations accurately.
Identify targets for feedback after marking.
c: This lesson uses a 45-minute independent assessment. Follow your teacher's instructions on access to notes, timing and permitted resources.
State = brief fact. Describe = give relevant detail. Explain = link the cause/feature to its effect. Compare = show a relevant similarity or difference.
Use the number of marks to decide how many distinct points and explanations are needed. Write clearly and directly.
Do not reveal model answers during the timed section. After the assessment, use the separate answer-review resource when your teacher allows it.

m.title: How to explain a mark scheme
m.q: A familiar practice question asks: explain why a larger cache can improve CPU performance. [2 marks] How would you plan TWO linked points? This is not an assessment question.
st: The command word is 'explain', so a definition alone is insufficient.
A larger cache holds more frequently used data/instructions [1].
This reduces the need for slower access to RAM [1].
Two linked ideas gain two marks. Do not write this model for an unrelated question.

w: Practice only: a single school building needs to share a printer. Give TWO reasons to use a LAN. [2 marks]
LAN covers a small geographical area [1]; its devices can share a network printer [1].
Practice only: a school receives a fake password-reset email. State the likely attack and one warning sign. [2 marks]
Phishing [1]; suspicious link, urgency or unexpected request for credentials [1].
Practice only: explain one benefit of adding CPU cores when running several applications. [2 marks]
Different cores may process more tasks simultaneously [1], improving multitasking [1].
wSteps: Start from the geographical area and resource.
LAN covers a small geographical area [1]; its devices can share a network printer [1].
Identify a social-engineering term and evidence.
Phishing [1]; suspicious link, urgency or unexpected request for credentials [1].
Link core count to workload, not guaranteed speed.
Additional cores can handle separate tasks [1].
Different cores may process more tasks simultaneously [1], improving multitasking [1].

k.q: Assessment coding question: independently predict, trace and change the supplied OCR ERL program. Do not run code until instructed.
k.code:
accessLevel = 1
if accessLevel > 1 then
    print("Staff access")
else
    print("Standard access")
endif
p: Change accessLevel to 2; state the new output. [1 mark]
Write a second IF statement that prints "Extra check" when accessLevel is greater than 2. [2 marks]
k.a:
With accessLevel = 1: Standard access [1]. With 2: Staff access [1].

Possible extension:
if accessLevel > 2 then
    print("Extra check")
endif

Award [1] for correct IF condition and [1] for printing the specified message with correct OCR ERL syntax. Model scheme for original practice.

e:
Assessment Q1. State what LAN and WAN mean, and identify the device that forwards data between networks. [3 marks]

Source: Original J277-style assessment question, not an OCR past-paper original.
Local Area Network [1]; Wide Area Network [1]; router [1].

Assessment Q2. A public library uses a school-style star LAN to share files and printers. Explain one advantage of the topology and one potential weakness. [4 marks]

Source: Original J277-style assessment question, not an OCR past-paper original.

Central switch simplifies adding/managing devices [1], allowing easier administration [1]. The central switch is a single point of failure [1], so if it fails connected devices may be unable to communicate [1].

Assessment Q3. A student is sent a fake link asking for school credentials. Explain the threat and TWO protective measures. [6 marks]

Source: Original J277-style assessment question, not an OCR past-paper original.

Phishing/social engineering [1] tricks users with a false link or identity [1]. Training helps recognise/report suspicious messages [1], reducing credential disclosure [1]. Two-factor authentication adds separate proof [1], reducing risk when a password is stolen [1].
v: Give a correct fact with little or no elaboration.
Give a reason and link it to an outcome.
Number of available marks guiding answer detail.
Work completed without coaching or model answers during the test.
x: For a four-mark explain question, listing one unsupported fact always earns full marks.
r: A message impersonates a bank and requests a password. Name the threat. [1 mark]
State what encryption does to data. [2 marks]
Transforms readable plaintext [1] into unreadable ciphertext without the correct key [1].
Monitors/filters network traffic [1] according to rules to block unauthorised traffic [1].
Explain two consequences of a denial-of-service attack on a school website. [4 marks]
Service becomes overloaded/unavailable [1], preventing legitimate users from accessing learning materials [1]. Repeated disruption may waste staff time [1] and interrupt lessons or operations [1].
